newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Thomson rates Lithuania, Lithuanian Vilnius Bank.
newsitem.headline: Thomson rates Lithuania, Lithuanian Vilnius Bank.

text.p: New York-based ratings agency Thomson BankWatch said on Thursday it has given Lithuania a sovereign risk rating of BB-, the second international credit rating it has received.
Thomson also said in a statement it has assigned to leading bank Vilnius Bank a short-term local currency debt rating of LC-1, the highest, and a BB- for long-term local currency debt.

"Although a recovery is currently underway, the economy remains fragile and is still feeling the effects of last year's banking sector crisis," Thomson BankWatch director of sovereign risk Betty Starkey said in the statement.
Moody's recently assigned a Ba2 to Lithuania's foreign currency debt and a Ba3 to its bank deposits.
The country's neighbours Latvia and Estonia have also said they would like to have international debt ratings.

Starkey pointed out that the economic prospects for the former Soviet country were improving, helped by a stable exchange rate, falling inflation and interest rates, a manageable external deficit and relatively low foreign debt.

She also said cautious budgetary policies were helping to rein in fiscal imbalances, despite pressures from low tax revenues, continued domestic subsidies, rising state company debt and costs of the bank crisis.
"Going forward, further progress toward privatisation and industrial restructuring will be critical to sustaining and accelerating the country's economic momentum," she added.
Thomson said Vilnius Bank's rating was due to its emergence as the largest and strongest private bank, most of which is owned by Western capital.
"Management is highly regarded and appears professional innovative and conservative," Thomson's Ramin Habibi said.
"The bank's earnings are satisfactory, and the outlook for 1996 appears favourable," he added.
He said the LC-1 short-term local currency rating was due to the bank's prudence and Thomson's belief that it would continue to develop as a major player.
